content.text: tetany: calcium gluconate 10 mL 10% solution IV over 10 min - response can be dramatic but may last only few hrs; may need repeat boluses or 20 to 30 mL 10% calcium gluconate in 1 L D5W over 12 to 24 h; hazardous w digoxin: give slowly w cont ECG monitoring after checking for (& correcting) hypokalemia
Calcium gluconate in NaCl inj dose, acute Sxtomatic hypocalcemia (adults):
Adults: initial dose 1,000 mg to 2,000 mg. Subsequent doses 1,000 mg to 2,000 mg every 6 h if needed. Cont infusion: initiate @ 5.4 mg/kg/h to 21.5 mg/kg/h. Bolus rate: ⍉ exceed 200 mg/min in adults
Calcium gluconate in NaCl inj safety:

CI: hypercalcemia. CI: neonates (28 days of age or younger) receiving ceftriaxone. ⍉in pts receiving ♡ glycosides; if necessary, give slowly in sm amounts w close ECG monitoring. ⍉ give ceftriaxone simultaneously w calcium via a Y-site in any age group. Calcinosis cutis can occur w or w.o extravasation; tissue necrosis · ulceration and 2ndry infect are the most serious comp. If extravasation or calcinosis cutis signs occur, stop IV @ that site STAT & tx prn. Rapid inj may cause vasodilate · ↓BP · brady · arrhythmias · syncope and ♡ arrest; infuse slowly. Measure serum Ca every 4 to 6 h during intermittent infusions & every 1 to 4 h during cont infusion. OD may cause hypercalcemia; Sx develop when total serum Ca = ≥12 mg/dL. If OD occurs, stop administration STAT & give supportive tx to restore intravasc vol & promote urinary Ca excretion if needed
